chunk_map.heading: I don't often know what is right and wrong

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L6 'This new field just throws my old skills off.' comes closest: 'this new field' is not named in this file or the neighbouring slide (L1 of i-wanted-to-be-right.md), but the deck is a guide's first-person passage inside a lecture on agentic product work, the phrase is a verbatim public-post quote under a quote-only guard, and no reader is left holding a wrong referent. 'I' is the guide, set by the lecture. Harm (an unresolvable pronoun) not present.
No pointer to another file or slide by position; closest L4-8 are all first-person statements with no callback.

rules_evaluated.na_reason: no 'the X you did/saw' backward references

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no demo beat, guess cue or reveal

rules_evaluated.evidence: L4-8 carry a self-sufficient claim: the guide has tried, mostly failed, and cannot tell right from wrong. Not a wait-state slide.
Header L1 'I don't often know what is right and wrong' is repeated in L6 and the three paragraphs are the failures, the confusion and the shared condition; the content does not contradict it.
Closest L4 'I have tried things. I have built things.' is a two-leg pair, below the anaphora-triple threshold; no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.', no superlative, no number, no abstraction stack, no verb triplet.
